claim: For the standard 4-simplex \(\Delta_4=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:x_j\ge0,\sum_jx_j\le1\}\), the Fourier transform \(F(k)=\int_{\Delta_4}e^{-2\pi i\langle k,x\rangle}\,dx\) at \(k\in\mathbb Z^4\) vanishes exactly when the multiset \(\{0,k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4\}\) has five distinct entries or has the form \(\{a,a,a+d,a+2d,a+2d\}\) for integers \(a\) and \(d\ne0\); this is the first simplex dimension with a repeated-node lattice zero.
integrity: The infinite classification follows from an exact confluent divided-difference/residue proof and the transcendence of pi. A standalone exact-arithmetic checker tests a bounded set of integer multisets only as a diagnostic. Independent mathematical audit has not been performed.
scientific_limitations: Only the integer-frequency zero set of the standard 4-simplex is classified; no claim is made for arbitrary simplex shapes, noninteger frequencies, or dimensions five and higher.
title: A first repeated-node resonance in the lattice Fourier zeros of the standard 4-simplex
